samples.marker_line: OFX ransomware: extorts files; adds RAT and evasion traits
Red Hat API helpers: configured requests; registry-identical code
Red Hat UI utilities: same-origin exports; fixes name-only identity

native_reverse_engineering.identification: Unsigned Windows x64 OFX ransomware and Discord-controlled RAT; version resources claim Microsoft Windows System Cache (syscache.exe).
native_reverse_engineering.file_encryption: Main 0x140016d20 creates a 32-byte session key and 12-byte nonce. 0x1400036c0 selects AES/GCM; 0x140003830 encrypts buffers. File worker calls it at 0x140006676 and 0x1400067d0, writes ciphertext through the resolved NtWriteFile wrapper and marks the original for deletion with FileDispositionInformation at 0x1400068a1. File enumeration skips system/program paths and handles .ofx output.
native_reverse_engineering.key_and_extortion: 0x140003920 imports an RSA-2048 public blob and seals the 32-byte session key using OAEP/SHA-256. 0x1400160a0 constructs YOUR FILES ARE ENCRYPTED with the sealed key and conditions decryptor release on payment. Main distributes notes to selected roots and the user Desktop.
native_reverse_engineering.control_channel: 0x140014bb0 queries Discord message history; main calls it before the task loop. Dispatcher 0x1400131f0 handles !info, !key, !unlock, !cat, !dl, !up, !exec, !screen, !wall, !sleep, !exit. Bot authorization, user/guild/channel API routes and message polls establish Discord API use.
native_reverse_engineering.shell_and_payloads: !exec appends supplied command text to cmd.exe /c, invokes 0x140012340 and returns captured pipe output. !up downloads a URL to a temporary .exe via 0x140011e10 and calls CreateProcessW at 0x140014332. No final downloaded payload is embedded or required to establish the command capability.
native_reverse_engineering.file_and_screen_export: !dl opens and reads an operator-selected file, then calls 0x140010bb0, which builds Discord multipart files[0]/payload_json requests. !screen calls GDI capture/PNG encoding at 0x14000e5a0, stages a temporary PNG, sends the same file through 0x140010bb0 and deletes it at 0x1400146c6. Startup also sends a host profile, encryption counts, sealed key and screenshot.
native_reverse_engineering.persistence: 0x1400161f0 obtains its own module path, creates an application-data location, copies itself at 0x1400167db, reconstructs Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run and writes the copied path under HKCU at 0x140016a49. The rule decodes the entire key path, not a campaign filename.
native_reverse_engineering.concealment_and_anti_analysis: The byte codec uses state=(seed-index*multiplier)&0xffffffff and XOR with (state^(state>>15))&255. Both operands vary by string. Decoded targets include NtQueryInformationProcess, analysis-injected DLL names, AmsiScanBuffer, EtwEventWrite and NT file/timing APIs. Manual PE export walking hashes names with FNV-1a. Main checks debugger state/debug registers, Wine, debugger windows, minimum uptime/CPU/RAM/screen resources and analysis modules before proceeding.
native_reverse_engineering.security_patches: 0x140017daa writes mov eax,0x80070057;ret over resolved AmsiScanBuffer after VirtualProtect. 0x140017f3b writes xor eax,eax;ret over resolved EtwEventWrite. The new API matchers verify decoded plaintext using operand values and initialized stack slots; composites also require the matching write stub and page-protection capability.
native_reverse_engineering.verdict_basis: Bulk destructive encryption plus a payment demand, remote shell/file/screen tasks, covert reactivation and security-control patches overwhelmingly support MALICIOUS. No legitimate product purpose or authorized deployment is supplied. The sandbox rating was corroborative, not the basis of the static claims.

npm_reverse_engineering.javascript-clients-shared: Exact registry tarball SHA-256 match. Reviewed all five runtime modules and source maps. Configuration stores caller-provided API keys/passwords/tokens and optional getters; authConfig formats request headers/query/options; sendRequest and createRequestFunction send to caller-configured base paths. APIFactory wraps supplied action functions. No install hook or additional code stage. The example.com URL is a URL-construction placeholder.
npm_reverse_engineering.frontend-components-utilities: Exact registry tarball SHA-256 match. Reviewed ESM/CJS implementations, testing helpers, 88 source maps, manifests and exports. PDF export POSTs caller-provided service/template/settings to /api/crc-pdf-generator/v1/generate on window.location.origin, converts the response to a Blob and triggers a browser save. Other modules implement Redux state/middleware, UI routing, RBAC checks, batched caller functions, CSV/JSON saves and Sentry error reporting. Browser platform APIs and the parent application supply dynamic inventory/auth context.
npm_reverse_engineering.direct_dependency_followup: Forager recovered exact npm originals for axios 1.20.0, tslib 2.8.1, @redhat-cloud-services/rbac-client 2.2.11, @redhat-cloud-services/types 2.0.3, @sentry/browser 7.120.4, awesome-debounce-promise 2.1.0, commander 2.20.3, mkdirp 1.0.4, p-map 7.1.1 and react-content-loader 6.2.1. Scanned all ten, inventoried runtime entry points/lifecycle scripts/URL and execution leads, and reviewed relevant implementations. Commander child_process.spawn dispatches explicit CLI subcommands; Sentry POSTs configured error events; Axios evil.com text is an anti-prototype-pollution comment. No malicious dependency behavior found in the reviewed paths.
npm_reverse_engineering.limits: Semver ranges resolve at review time; there is no lockfile or installed dependency tree to reconstruct a historical deployment. Peer frameworks and runtime endpoints depend on the consuming application. These artifacts themselves implement ordinary library functionality.
npm_reverse_engineering.possible_external_mislabel: The source did not supply the basis for the npm labels. API credential fields, browser file saves/JSON POSTs, empty author fields and monorepo name/repository differences are plausible heuristic leads; claiming which one caused the label would be speculation. Official registry byte identity and traced caller-driven behavior tip both verdicts to BENIGN.

rule_review.identity_correction: Moved the exact manifest-name matcher from well-known/lib/ui/redhat-frontend-components::utilities-package-name to metadata/package/name/identity::redhat-frontend-utilities-name. The matcher and notable criticality are unchanged. It proves a name declaration, not the library implementation. Repository-wide YAML/reference search found no consumers of the old identity. Positive and differently named manifest controls passed. The old identity is the only lost finding, replaced in the archive root and package.json by the correctly placed declaration.
rule_review.behavior_losses: None. All pre-existing OFX traits and all shared-package findings remain; all other frontend findings remain. No suppressions or severity reductions were introduced.
rule_review.coverage_limit: Native matchers cover the observed x64 compiler/decoder shapes and variable keys, not every possible implementation. Some broader capabilities, including URL-fetched payload execution, are visible through retained primitives and the RAT tasking detection rather than a separately path-bound payload-chain rule. A trial generic executed-payload/status composite was rejected because its static requirements did not bind the downloaded path to CreateProcess; no unsupported chain claim was retained.
rule_review.hostile_goal: Seven distinct supported hostile results: extortion encryption, Discord shell tasking, AMSI patch, ETW patch, screen upload, file upload and Run-key reactivation. The count exceeds the guidance because each result is separately evidenced.
